title: Founding of Calamba
description: Calamba is established as a separate town by Franciscan missionaries, separated from the older town of Tabuco (now Cabuyao). The name is said to derive from a large clay water jar ('kalan-banga') that became a symbol of the town.

title: Birth of Dr. José Rizal
description: On June 19, the Philippines' national hero Dr. José Protasio Rizal Mercado y Alonso Realonda is born in the Mercado-Rizal ancestral house in Calamba, an event that would forever link the town to the country's struggle for independence.

title: Confiscation of the Friar Lands
description: The Dominican-administered Calamba Hacienda forcibly displaces tenant farmers, including the Mercado-Rizal family, foreshadowing the agrarian conflict Rizal would later expose in his novels and writings.

title: Calambeños Join the Revolution
description: Townspeople of Calamba take part in the Philippine Revolution against Spain and the subsequent Philippine–American War, contributing to the wider struggle for national independence.

title: Reconstruction of the Rizal Shrine
description: Reconstruction of the Mercado-Rizal ancestral home begins under the National Historical Committee, restoring the birthplace of Dr. José Rizal as a national shrine and museum (completed 1950).

title: Liberation from Japanese Occupation
description: Calamba is liberated by combined Filipino and American forces during the closing months of World War II, after suffering significant destruction during the war years.

title: Resort Capital of the Philippines
description: Calamba is officially recognized as the 'Resort Capital of the Philippines', anchored by its world-renowned hot spring resorts in Pansol, Bucal, and Bagong Kalsada drawn from the geothermal waters of Mount Makiling.

title: Conversion to a Component City
description: Republic Act No. 9024 is ratified on April 21 via plebiscite, converting the Municipality of Calamba into a Component City of Laguna and ushering in expanded fiscal autonomy and urban development.

title: Calamba as Provincial Capital of Laguna
description: Republic Act No. 9495 formally designates Calamba as the new capital of the Province of Laguna, transferring provincial seat functions from Santa Cruz and reinforcing the city's role as a regional center.

title: 150th Birth Anniversary of José Rizal
description: Calamba hosts national commemorations for the 150th birth anniversary of Dr. José Rizal, including the unveiling of one of the tallest Rizal monuments in the country at the city plaza.

title: Pandemic Response and Recovery
description: The City Government leads frontline response efforts during the COVID-19 pandemic, scaling up health services, social amelioration programs, and digital service delivery across all 54 barangays.

title: 12th Sangguniang Panlungsod
description: Following the May 2025 national and local elections, Mayor Roseller 'Ross' Rizal, Vice Mayor Angelito 'Totie' Lazaro Jr., and the 12th Sangguniang Panlungsod assume office for the 2025–2028 term.
